themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors, aggressive enforcement action, or organized street vending activity that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average per week over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, severity high)
Represents the freshest spike in the dataset with the highest statistical z-score
Aligns with community board's standing request for more frequent litter basket collection, suggesting sanitation infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food vendors proliferating in specific neighborhoods (Fort Washington Ave, Broadway corridor)? Interview street vendors and DOHMH.
Is the city's street vending licensing process creating bottlenecks that push vendors underground?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaint Wave
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Ubers, Lyft, black cars) spiked to 18 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 1.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 860% increase—indicating congestion, traffic safety, or parking conflicts concentrated in the last 7 days.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 1.9 average per week over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.1, severity high)
Second-highest z-score in dataset, indicating statistically exceptional spike
Overlaps with chronic illegal parking complaints (2,619 over 90 days), suggesting systemic transit/parking pressure
reporting_angles: Map the geographic hotspots: are complaints concentrated near transit hubs (181st St subway), hospitals, or commercial corridors?
Interview residents about safety concerns: near-miss accidents, double-parked vehicles blocking emergency access, sidewalk congestion from pickups/dropoffs.
Query TLC data on for-hire vehicle volume growth in CD 112 over the same timeframe.

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 21 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 4.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% spike—pointing to accelerating pavement deterioration, tripping hazards, or ADA accessibility failures that demand immediate DOT inspection.
evidence: 21 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 4.4 average per week over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.64, severity high)
Compounds with street sweeping complaints UP 395% (13 last week vs. 2.6 avg), suggesting systemic sanitation/maintenance failure
Aligns with community board's standing requests for street/sidewalk infrastructure investment—unsolved multi-year problem
reporting_angles: Physical canvass: photograph specific blocks with the highest complaint concentration (cross-reference addresses); document tripping hazards, broken concrete, accessibility violations.
Elderly/disabled residents: interview seniors about fall risks and ADA compliance issues; consult NYC Comptroller's Office for DOT capital budget allocation to CD 112.
Is this a leading indicator of more severe street infrastructure decay to come?

themes_detail.label: Dead and Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% spike—signaling possible disease, pest outbreak, or neglect in Parks maintenance that could threaten canopy cover and pedestrian safety.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 average per week over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.21, severity high)
Aligns with community board's repeated budget requests for park safety and park reconstruction/upgrades—indicating systemic underinvestment
Complements street sweeping and sidewalk complaints to paint picture of environmental neglect
reporting_angles: Partner with Parks Dept to identify affected tree locations and species; investigate whether a specific pest, disease (e.g., emerald ash borer), or drought stress is driving the spike.
Interview environmental advocates: are tree planting and maintenance budgets inadequate for CD 112 relative to other districts?
Canopy equity angle: does Washington Heights/Inwood have lower tree cover than comparable neighborhoods?

themes_detail.label: Industrial Waste Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Industrial waste complaints jumped to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,100% spike—indicating possible illegal dumping, construction debris mishandling, or environmental violations that warrant immediate investigation by DSNY and DEC.
evidence: 3 industrial waste complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.16, severity high)
368 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (318 alterations, 24 new buildings) suggest active construction that may be generating debris improperly
Potential environmental justice issue in a residential neighborhood with high density housing
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 industrial waste complaint addresses with DOB permit locations; identify whether specific construction projects are violating waste disposal rules.
Interview DSNY and DEC on enforcement activity; obtain violation notices issued to contractors or property owners in past 2 weeks.
Environmental health angle: what are health risks to residents from illegal dumping near homes?
